increments.change: Native cylinders against cylinders with nonparallel axes, spheres centred off the cylinder axis, and ring tori that are off-axis or tilted now return complete exact results instead of UnsupportedIntersection. An exact rational height H bounds every common point (|h| s <= R1 + R2 + |o1 - o2|_1 for cylinder pairs with s = |a1 x a2|; |a.(c - o)| + radius for spheres and tori), found by exact doubling. The cylinder portion |h| <= H is covered by ten rational quadratic tensor patches whose seam points have half-angle tangents 0, +/-5/12, +/-3/4, +/-4/3, +/-12/5 and infinity, so every seam point, middle control and weight is rational in the cylinder frame; each patch is sectioned by the complete implicit/tensor route. The result publishes the exact tensor-image pieces and deduplicated isolated points, with both operand pcurves typed unavailable because the atlas is an internal chart. Pieces meet at atlas seams that are not physical vertices and depend on which cylinder is charted. The existing parallel and coaxial special routes are dispatched exactly as before. The tensor-image contact route also gains an exact gradient fallback for contacts at topology events: at a regular point of the source's defining equation f, the contact is tangent exactly when f_u G_v - f_v G_u vanishes, evaluated as rational forms at the selected UV point; singular points stay typed. increments.change: Ring tori against spheres centred off the torus axis and against non-coaxial cones now return complete exact results instead of UnsupportedIntersection. increments.change: The torus atlas route's stress cost came from merging seam points, not from sectioning (each patch takes about 0.1 s): exact comparisons of distinct high-degree selected points took 12-49 s each. Three sound reductions remove almost all of them. (1) Atlas patches are injective charts whose images meet only along shared boundaries: results of one patch are already distinct, and results of different patches are compared only when both lie on their patch's UV boundary. (2) The torus atlas supplies its exact arc adjacency (patch_contact): patches in non-consecutive arcs have disjoint closed images, consecutive major arcs share a v boundary, consecutive minor arcs a u boundary, and doubly consecutive patches only a corner, so comparisons require the matching boundary coordinates. (3) GeometricPoint3::coincides_with first compares two rational-surface points along the generic direction (1, 1/3, 1/7); a decided difference proves distinctness before any shared coordinate is proved equal. increments.change: Tensor-graph solids gain exact volume when the top is a polynomial tensor (equal weights) whose face is trimmed by UV segments. With frame coordinates a = A/(det w0), b = B/(det w0), c = C/(det w0), the volume is |det(u, v, d)| times the integral over the trimmed UV region of c |d(a, b)/d(u, v)| = C J / (det w0)^3 with J = A_u B_v - A_v B_u; Green's theorem turns it into -sum of integral H du over the face's oriented boundary segments (H the v-antiderivative of C J), each integrated exactly as a polynomial in the segment parameter. The integrand has one sign (positive heights, injective projection), so the absolute value is the volume. Rational tops or curved trims report UnsupportedMeasurement.
